links.outcome: Reasoning truthfulness and accuracy when grounding intermediate steps in a structured evidence graph with a hallucination detector
links.effect: Accuracy improved by up to 12.7% on six medical benchmarks; blind physician evaluations showed substantially increased reasoning truthfulness without loss of informational content.
links.quote: Blind physician evaluations confirm that MedMMV substantially increases reasoning truthfulness without sacrificing informational content.

unlisted_practices: Diversified short rollouts to stabilize early evidence interpretation in multimodal reasoning
Multi-agent hallucination detector supervising intermediate reasoning steps
Combined uncertainty scorer to aggregate candidate reasoning paths

screen.reason: The paper introduces and benchmarks a novel multi-agent MLLM architecture (MedMMV) using benchmarks and blind physician evaluations to reduce hallucination and reasoning instability. Developing and benchmarking a new agent framework is model/system architecture research rather than testing an organizational deployment safeguard or practice.
